case-sara.text: [Softly] Seeing his name pop up still throws me, and I hate how much it matters.
case-sara.suggestion: Seeing his name still throws you, and you hate that it matters so much. Could we pause with that feeling for a moment and notice what is here now?

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I tell friends I'm fine, and then I worry they can hear that I am not.
case-sara.suggestion: You try to sound fine, and it feels risky that they might hear how not fine you are. Find the moment when being heard starts to feel dangerous.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I feel lost after the breakup, like I do not know what to do with the evenings.
case-sara.suggestion: The evenings are where the lostness shows up most clearly. Bring one evening close and sense what feels hardest when there is nowhere to put yourself.

case-sara.text: [Softly] I wrote 'sorry' to him three times, then realized I do not know what I was trying to fix.
case-sara.suggestion: Writing sorry was a reach toward repair, and then the ground disappeared under what you were trying to fix. Slow down at that unclear place and see which feeling appears.

case-sara.text: [Panicked] I delete photos to prove I am done, then panic and look for them again.
case-sara.suggestion: One move says, 'be done,' and then the panic says this ending is not that simple. Pause in the moment between deleting and searching.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When someone is kind to me, my eyes drop before I can stop it.
case-sara.suggestion: Your eyes drop as soon as someone is kind. Could we slow that moment down and notice what you feel as you receive the kindness?

case-sara.text: [Softly] For a few seconds after I wake up, I forget he is gone, and then I remember.
case-sara.suggestion: There is that brief relief, and then the loss returns all at once. Let the moment of remembering be here before you have to do anything with it.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I am sad, and then I get embarrassed that I am still talking about it.
case-sara.suggestion: Sadness is here, and embarrassment quickly asks whether you should still be talking about it. Give both a little room and notice which one is stronger now.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] When I see couples holding hands, I get upset and then feel childish for wanting that.
case-sara.suggestion: Seeing them brings up the wanting, and then shame moves in around the wanting. Keep close to the wanting for a moment before shame moves in.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] If I let someone see the whole mess, I imagine them quietly wishing I would stop.
case-sara.suggestion: Part of you wants someone to see how bad it is, and another part expects them to wish you would stop. Track that pull between wanting to be seen and expecting rejection.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I had something funny to tell him on the bus. For a moment I forgot we weren't together. Remembering was the sad part.
case-sara.suggestion: The sadness arrives when you remember you can't tell him. Could we stay for a moment with how that lands now?

case-sara.text: [Softly] My sister didn't tell me to move on. She just stayed. I felt relieved, and I think there's more to it than that.
case-sara.suggestion: There's relief in her simply staying. Take a little time with that relief and see what else you notice.

case-michael.text: [Firm] When someone corrects one detail, I keep hearing it afterward like I was called out.
case-michael.suggestion: The correction stays with you as though you were called out. As you say that now, what do you notice in yourself?

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] I walk into meetings already ready for somebody to disrespect me.
case-michael.suggestion: You enter already on guard, before anything has happened. Let yourself feel what it is like to walk in already ready for disrespect.

case-michael.text: [Tense] After I blow up at home, I tell myself they pushed me, but I still feel lousy.
case-michael.suggestion: One part says they pushed you, and another part is left with that lousy feeling afterward. Keep close to the lousy feeling before the argument about blame takes over.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] Sometimes I want to throw my phone after a work message, and then I feel ridiculous.
case-michael.suggestion: The urge comes fast, and then you are left looking at yourself with shame. Pause with the shame that follows, just before it calls you ridiculous.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] A small sigh from my wife can feel like she has already decided I am the problem.
case-michael.suggestion: That small sigh lands like a decision has already been made about you. Slow down at the first flare and notice what it says you are being accused of.

case-michael.text: [Tense] When I do not know the answer, I get tense and start talking like I know anyway.
case-michael.suggestion: You get tense just before you start sounding certain. Could we pause with that tension and notice what it is like not to have the answer?

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] I reread every message before sending because one mistake will bother me all night.
case-michael.suggestion: One possible mistake can stay with you for hours, so the checking becomes hard to stop. Find the first moment when checking starts to feel necessary.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] The second I feel weak, I get angry and hear my dad saying that is exactly the problem.
case-michael.suggestion: 'Weak' brings anger and your father's judgment in very fast. Pause at the instant when weakness first shows up.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] Some nights I replay every word I said, trying to find where I messed it up.
case-michael.suggestion: You replay every word, looking for the moment you got it wrong. Sense what happens inside when you think you have found the mistake.

case-michael.text: [Vulnerable] I want my son to feel safe around me, and I do not know how to say that without sounding weak.
case-michael.suggestion: You want safety for him so much, and even naming that wish brushes against the old weakness rule. Let the wish itself have a moment before the rule closes around it.

case-michael.text: [Quietly] My son asked whether I'd be at his game. I said yes, but the way he asked made me sad. Like he couldn't quite count on it.
case-michael.suggestion: There's sadness in hearing that uncertainty from him. What is it like to let yourself notice it here, without fixing it straight away?

case-michael.text: [Frustrated, then hesitant] I was furious about the correction. Then I realised I was disappointed in myself as well. That bit is harder to talk about.
case-michael.suggestion: The disappointment in yourself is harder to approach. We can go slowly and stay with just the bit you can put words to.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When it is my turn to speak, I lose track of what I was going to say.
case-jason.suggestion: The words disappear when it is your turn. Could we take that moment slowly and notice what happens inside before you try to find the sentence again?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I hover over send, then delete the text because wanting contact suddenly feels humiliating.
case-jason.suggestion: The wish for contact is there, and humiliation makes the message hard to let exist. Keep the wanting in focus for a moment before the deleting happens.

case-jason.text: [Fearful] I got invited to a birthday party, and part of me was excited, but then I started worrying I would ruin it.
case-jason.suggestion: There is excitement about being invited, and then worry starts to crowd it. Give the excitement a little space before the worry crowds it.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] If I meet someone's eyes too long, I assume they can tell how awkward I am.
case-jason.suggestion: Eye contact starts to feel like they can see the awkwardness you are trying to hide. Hold on the first second of being seen.

case-jason.text: [Embarrassed] After meetings, one small awkward pause can make me cringe for the rest of the day.
case-jason.suggestion: That one pause keeps coming back long after the meeting. Slow it down and notice what the cringe says about how you think you were seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] When I walk into a room, I look for the exit before I decide whether to join anyone.
case-jason.suggestion: You look for the exit before you decide whether to join anyone. Could we pause at that moment and notice what you feel as you look around?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Before I introduce myself, I start imagining how strange I will sound.
case-jason.suggestion: Even before you speak, the moment is already becoming a test of how you will come across. Pause before the introduction and sense the imagined strangeness.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I compare myself to everyone there and always decide I am the least interesting person.
case-jason.suggestion: The comparison ends with you at the bottom, and it hurts before anyone has actually rejected you. Let that hurt have a moment.

case-jason.text: [Blank] Sometimes I pretend to text so small talk does not have to start.
case-jason.suggestion: The phone gives you a way to pause the contact, and a little cover from being put on the spot. See what happens just before you reach for that cover.

case-jason.text: [Quiet and ashamed] I felt lonely on Sunday, but I also ignored two messages.
case-jason.suggestion: Loneliness and pulling back sit side by side. Keep close to the loneliness that is there even while the messages go unanswered.

case-jason.text: [Quietly pleased] They asked me to join them again. I felt pleased when I read it. Then I started worrying about what I'd say.
case-jason.suggestion: Before the worry arrived, there was that pleased feeling. Could we give it a little room and notice what being invited again was like?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I wish my friend had waited for me after the meeting. I don't usually admit wishing for things like that. It feels a bit sad saying it.
case-jason.suggestion: Saying you wanted him to wait brings some sadness. You don't have to explain it away; we can listen to what that sadness is like.

case-arne.text: [Softly] There’s sadness right here when I picture the empty chair.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we stay a moment with that sadness and see what you notice?

case-arne.text: [Voice catches] I wanted to tell her the gate was fixed. I still want to.
case-arne.suggestion: That wish to tell her is here now. What is it like to let yourself hear it?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] My chest aches when I remember her laughing.
case-arne.suggestion: As you remember that laugh, what happens in the ache?

case-arne.text: [Frowning] I feel angry about being told to be grateful.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we give that anger a little room? What is it objecting to?

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I just want someone to ask how my day was.
case-arne.suggestion: That wish feels close now. What is it like to say it here?

case-arne.text: [Softly] My shoulders loosen when I say I was tired too.
case-arne.suggestion: Could you notice that loosening for a moment? What feels different?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’m lonely tonight. It’s hard to say so plainly.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay with those plain words. What do you notice as you say “lonely”?

case-arne.text: [Tearful smile] Remembering her teasing me feels warm for a moment.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we pause with that warmth before we go on?

case-arne.text: [Steady] I’m sad, but I don’t feel ashamed saying it here.
case-arne.suggestion: What is it like to have the sadness here without that shame?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] That guilt comes as soon as I remember enjoying myself.
case-arne.suggestion: When the guilt arrives, what does it seem to say about enjoying yourself?

case-arne.text: [Softly] I feel grateful that Tom stayed, and sad that I needed it.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we hear both—being glad he stayed, and the sadness beside it?

case-arne.text: [Sighs] Saying “I loved her” brings the tears closer.
case-arne.suggestion: We can take that slowly. What happens as you say those words?

case-arne.text: [Softly] The peace at breakfast feels good, then I tighten up.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we pause at that tightening and notice what comes with it?

case-arne.text: [Voice lowers] I miss her, but the hospital nights—there’s anger there too.
case-arne.suggestion: If you want, we can give that anger room without losing the missing. What is it about?

case-arne.text: [Half-smile] Her teasing still makes me laugh. Then the empty room hits me.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we take that turn slowly, from the laugh to noticing the room?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I needed Emma to see me, not take over. Saying that feels prickly.
case-arne.suggestion: What do you notice in that prickly feeling as you name what you needed?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] Saying I was exhausted brings ease, then a voice calling me selfish.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we hear the ease first, before that judgment takes all the room?

case-arne.text: [Tearful smile] I was happy at the workshop. There’s sadness right next to it.
case-arne.suggestion: What is it like to let the happiness and sadness be here together?

case-arne.text: [Frowning] I wanted her to understand how tired I was. I feel bad wanting that.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we stay with wanting to be understood, before deciding it was bad?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I miss being useful to her. I don’t miss being needed every minute.
case-arne.suggestion: What is it like to hear that difference in your own words?

case-arne.text: [Looks down] Tom stayed without asking anything. My chest softened, then I nearly cried.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we notice that softening and what his staying meant, at your pace?

case-arne.text: [Softly] I’m angry when they decide what Eva would want. Underneath, I think I miss her.
case-arne.suggestion: We can hear both. Where would you like to stay a little—the anger or the missing?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] Putting the coat away gave me room. Then I wanted it back.
case-arne.suggestion: What did having that room feel like before the wish to bring it back?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] “I’m lonely” feels true. It also sounds like asking too much.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we give the true part a moment? What is it like to say you’re lonely here?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] That ease is real, but I don’t want it called freedom from Eva.
case-arne.suggestion: What is the ease like in your own terms, without that label?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] There’s anger here. I’m not ready to find the sadness underneath.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay with the anger itself. What does it want heard, if you want to explore it?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] Something softened when I said I needed rest. Now I feel watched again.
case-arne.suggestion: Let’s pause. What would help you feel less watched here?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] I’m touched by the memory. Please don’t ask me to make it bigger.
case-arne.suggestion: We can leave it at this size. Would quietly noticing it feel right, or would you rather go on?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] It’s tenderness, perhaps. Saying that makes me want to joke.
case-arne.suggestion: We can notice that urge without removing it. Is a small moment with the tenderness welcome?

case-arne.text: [Steady] I’m sad, and I don’t need to go into the old scene to know it.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay with the sadness here, without the scene. What do you want me to hear of it?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] I said shame, but the word doesn’t fit now. Something is still there.
case-arne.suggestion: We can leave “shame” aside. What do you notice of the something that remains?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’m pleased about the workshop. I don’t want to defend that pleasure.
case-arne.suggestion: You needn’t defend it. Would you like room to notice what was pleasing, without an argument?

case-arne.text: [Frowning] I feel the tightness. Asking about it again makes it tighter.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll stop asking into it. Would you like quiet, or to turn toward something else?

case-arne.text: [Softly] I want company. That doesn’t mean I want every friend knowing the details.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we hear the kind of company you want, keeping those details private?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] The relief is here, and I’m checking whether you approve.
case-arne.suggestion: You don’t need my approval to have that feeling. What is it like to notice it without a verdict from me?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I miss the ordinary disagreements. I’m not sure why that feels tender.
case-arne.suggestion: We can be curious without deciding why. What is it like to remember one of those ordinary moments?

case-mia.text: [Sad] I feel sad right now, thinking about that unfinished drawing.
case-mia.suggestion: What part of the drawing are you missing as the sadness comes?

case-mia.text: [Angry] The anger is here when I remember being talked over.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we hear what that anger wants them to understand?

case-mia.text: [Relieved] There’s relief in saying I need the seat.
case-mia.suggestion: What is it like to let that need be said plainly?

case-mia.text: [Tearful] I miss being able to promise that I’ll come.
case-mia.suggestion: What hurts most about no longer being able to promise?

case-mia.text: [Softly] I feel warm remembering the visitor who wanted my opinion.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we pause with that warmth? What mattered about being asked?

case-mia.text: [Sad] I want someone to understand how much the ordinary things take.
case-mia.suggestion: As you say that wish here, what do you notice?

case-mia.text: [Guilty] The guilt arrives when I remember snapping at Alex.
case-mia.suggestion: What does the guilt say you wish you’d done differently?

case-mia.text: [Angry] I’m angry, and I know exactly which comment set it off.
case-mia.suggestion: What about that comment felt so wrong to you?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m scared of not knowing whether I’ll manage tomorrow.
case-mia.suggestion: What is the hardest part of that uncertainty right now?

case-mia.text: [Moved] Ella asked instead of assuming. I’m touched by that.
case-mia.suggestion: What did her asking give you in that moment?

case-mia.text: [Sad] I’m sad about needing help, even when the help is good.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we make room for what needing it brings up?

case-mia.text: [Steady] I feel calmer when I say I still get to choose.
case-mia.suggestion: What feels different when your choice has a place?

case-mia.text: [Sad, then laughs] I’m sad about the drawing. Ridiculous, really.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we hear what you’re sad to lose, before calling it ridiculous?

case-mia.text: [Angry, hesitant] I want my say. Then I hear myself sounding ungrateful.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we give the wish for a say a moment, before judging its tone?

case-mia.text: [Relieved, uneasy] It’s a relief to rest. And there’s this guilt beside it.
case-mia.suggestion: What is the guilt saying about the rest that you need?

case-mia.text: [Moved, cautious] I liked Sam asking my opinion. I don’t want to make too much of it.
case-mia.suggestion: What was good about being asked, even if we keep it a small moment?

case-mia.text: [Sad] Needing help hurts, even though I know I’d help Alex.
case-mia.suggestion: What feels painful about being the one receiving it now?

case-mia.text: [Angry, then lowers voice] I’m tired of explaining. Maybe I’m just being difficult.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we hear the tired-of-explaining part before calling it difficult?

case-mia.text: [Fearful] I’m scared I’ll lose more. I know worrying won’t prevent it.
case-mia.suggestion: Knowing that doesn’t remove the fear. What loss feels closest in it today?

case-mia.text: [Softly] There’s warmth when Alex stays beside me without doing anything. It feels odd.
case-mia.suggestion: What is it like to have that company without needing to make the moment useful?

case-mia.text: [Guilty] I regret the snapping, but not asking him to stop.
case-mia.suggestion: What becomes clearer when you separate the request from how it came out?

case-mia.text: [Sad, steady] I want to talk about what I miss, but not feel it in my body.
case-mia.suggestion: We can stay with words. What do you want us to hear about the missing?

case-mia.text: [Angry, uncertain] I feel angry with Ella. I also don’t want her to go.
case-mia.suggestion: What does the anger need from her while you still want her nearby?

case-mia.text: [Relieved] Saying “not today” feels easier here. Then I worry about tomorrow.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we notice what makes today’s no easier, without asking it to solve tomorrow?

case-mia.text: [Angry, uncertain] I’m cross with him. It might be about more than what he did.
case-mia.suggestion: As you notice the anger, what else comes to mind besides what he did?

case-mia.text: [Sad, firm] The sadness is here. I don’t want a deeper sadness found underneath it.
case-mia.suggestion: We can stay with this sadness as it is. What do you want heard in it?

case-mia.text: [Warm, uneasy] I felt close to Alex when he waited. Then I wanted to hurry him.
case-mia.suggestion: What became uncomfortable as you had that space to choose?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] The regret is clear. I don’t want it turned into a reason to stop being angry.
case-mia.suggestion: What does the regret ask you to change, while the anger still gets heard?

case-mia.text: [Moved, guarded] Being believed feels good. I’m waiting for the “but.”
case-mia.suggestion: What is it like right now to feel believed and still be waiting for that turn?

case-mia.text: [Sad, pauses] I miss it. I’m not even sure what “it” is today.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we stay with that missing without naming it too quickly? What comes to mind?

case-mia.text: [Angry, steady] I want the anger heard, not made useful.
case-mia.suggestion: What would being heard look like here, before we ask anything of the anger?

case-mia.text: [Relieved, confused] There’s relief when Alex leaves, and it makes me miss him.
case-mia.suggestion: How do the relief and missing sit together in that moment?

case-mia.text: [Softly] I’m glad I spoke at the meeting. Sadness came afterwards.
case-mia.suggestion: What does the sadness bring, alongside being glad you spoke?

case-mia.text: [Tired, emotional] I can feel this, but I can’t do much with it today.
case-mia.suggestion: We don’t need to do more with it. Would a few words about what’s here fit, or a pause?

case-mia.text: [Fearful] I’m scared of losing more. I don’t want guesses about how much I’ll lose.
case-mia.suggestion: We can stay with the fear without predicting losses. What is hard about holding it today?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] The feeling got less sharp when you said that. It didn’t go away.
case-mia.suggestion: What changed in the feeling when it became less sharp?

case-nora.text: [Hurt] It hurts when I remember him saying that about my face.
case-nora.suggestion: What is the most painful part as you remember it now?

case-nora.text: [Angry] The anger is here when I say “my work.”
case-nora.suggestion: What does that anger want heard about your work?

case-nora.text: [Sad] I miss looking forward to those meetings.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we hear what you miss about going into them?

case-nora.text: [Relieved] Saying it plainly feels like a relief.
case-nora.suggestion: What is different when you let yourself say it plainly?

case-nora.text: [Warm] I feel warm remembering Lina just staying with me.
case-nora.suggestion: What did her staying give you in that moment?

case-nora.text: [Fearful] I’m afraid I’ll become the complaint instead of the architect.
case-nora.suggestion: What is frightening about being seen that way?

case-nora.text: [Sad] I wanted them to ask me about the design.
case-nora.suggestion: What is it like to give that wish a voice here?

case-nora.text: [Angry] I’m angry that I have to explain my first answer.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we stay with what the repeated question does to you?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I’m ashamed of being upset.
case-nora.suggestion: What does the shame say being upset means about you?

case-nora.text: [Moved] I felt seen when someone asked for my opinion.
case-nora.suggestion: What part of you felt seen in being asked?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I feel calmer when I say I can choose when to respond.
case-nora.suggestion: What changes when the timing becomes yours to choose?

case-nora.text: [Sad] I’m sad, and I want it heard without advice.
case-nora.suggestion: We can leave advice aside. What do you want heard in the sadness?

case-nora.text: [Angry, then doubts] I want my own work seen. Maybe I’m making it all about me.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we hear that wish before judging whether it takes too much room?

case-nora.text: [Hurt] It hurt, and then I started defending why it should hurt.
case-nora.suggestion: What is it like to let the hurt be here without building its defense?

case-nora.text: [Relieved, guilty] Leaving the story alone tonight feels good and wrong.
case-nora.suggestion: What does the guilt say is wrong about taking that evening?

case-nora.text: [Sad, brisk] I miss trusting a meeting to be about the actual work. I know that sounds naive.
case-nora.suggestion: Before calling it naive, what do you miss in that trust?

case-nora.text: [Warm, wary] I felt included for a while. Part of me kept checking.
case-nora.suggestion: What was it like to enjoy that place while still checking it?

case-nora.text: [Angry, quieter] I’m angry with Max. I don’t want him gone.
case-nora.suggestion: What does the anger ask him to change while you still want his support?

case-nora.text: [Uneasy] I’m unsettled about today, even with the motive unclear.
case-nora.suggestion: What part of the unease can you name without deciding his motive?

case-nora.text: [Guilty] I regret the way I answered Adam, not being upset.
case-nora.suggestion: What becomes clearer when you separate those two?

case-nora.text: [Moved, hesitant] Being believed was good. I don’t want to make it a huge moment.
case-nora.suggestion: We can keep it small. What was good about being believed?

case-nora.text: [Sad, firm] I want to talk about the hurt, not search my body for it.
case-nora.suggestion: We can use words. What do you want us to hear in the hurt?

case-nora.text: [Fearful] I’m afraid they’ll see only a complaint. Then I feel ashamed of the fear.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we hear what is at stake in the fear before judging it?

case-nora.text: [Steady, emotional] Saying no to explaining feels better here than at work.
case-nora.suggestion: What makes that no feel more possible here?

case-nora.text: [Hurt, firm] The hurt is here. I don’t want you finding an older hurt to explain it.
case-nora.suggestion: We can stay with this hurt. What do you want heard in it?

case-nora.text: [Angry, uncertain] I’m angry with Max. The anger reaches further than what he said.
case-nora.suggestion: As you notice it, what else comes into view besides his words?

case-nora.text: [Sad, pauses] I miss something at work. I don’t know what to call it.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we give that missing a moment without naming it too quickly?

case-nora.text: [Relieved, guarded] I feel believed. I’m waiting for the part where I have to prove it again.
case-nora.suggestion: What is it like to feel believed here while still waiting for that turn?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] The regret is there. I don’t want it used to cancel the anger.
case-nora.suggestion: What does the regret ask you to change while the anger still gets heard?

case-nora.text: [Warm, serious] The enjoyment is small. It doesn’t need to become more than that.
case-nora.suggestion: What is good in that small enjoyment, if you want to stay with it?

case-nora.text: [Uneasy] I’m unsettled. I can explore that without guessing why he did it.
case-nora.suggestion: What part of the unease is available to put into words now?

case-nora.text: [Angry, steady] Don’t make the anger useful yet. Hear it first.
case-nora.suggestion: What would being heard look like here before we ask anything more of it?

case-nora.text: [Tired, emotional] I can feel it. I can’t make a coherent account of it.
case-nora.suggestion: You don’t need a coherent account. Would a few words fit, or a pause?

case-nora.text: [Softly] The hurt became less sharp. It didn’t become less true.
case-nora.suggestion: What changed in how you were carrying it when it became less sharp?

case-nora.text: [Fearful] I’m afraid of how they’ll respond. I don’t want predictions.
case-nora.suggestion: We can leave predictions aside. What is hardest about holding that uncertainty today?

case-nora.text: [Sad, steady] I want you to hear the loss without making it my whole identity.
case-nora.suggestion: Which part of the loss do you want heard on those terms?
